classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate same-arc angle transfers across two circles, recognise the supplementary angle at their connecting-line intersection, and select the triangle that determines x.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Nested circles with four outer vertices, an inner triangle and connecting chords. The inner circle's fourth incidence point lies at the crossing of the inner lower-left–outer right line and the outer upper-right–bottom chord. Internal coordinate names are not printed. No centre, concentricity, parallelism or numerical lengths are added.
spec.mathematics: The inner upper-left angle is 50 degrees. The inner angle at the fourth incidence point standing on the same chord is also 50 degrees. Its exterior angle in the triangle joining that point to the outer right and bottom vertices is 130 degrees. The outer bottom angle standing on the same chord as the given outer upper-left 10-degree angle is 10 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 10-degree and 50-degree angles and the unknown x are visible; the printed teacher answer is omitted.

answer.worked:
Let $H$ be the crossing of the two connecting lines on the smaller circle. The angle at $H$ standing on the same inner chord as the $50^\circ$ angle is $50^\circ$ (angles on the same arc).

The adjacent angle at $H$ in the triangle with the outer right and bottom vertices is $180^\circ-50^\circ=130^\circ$.

The angle at the outer bottom vertex is $10^\circ$ (angles on the same arc of the larger circle).

$$\begin{align*}x+130^\circ+10^\circ&=180^\circ\\x&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
